researchUpdates.title: Machine learning and Weibull-based reliability analysis of impact-resistant geopolymer concrete with construction demolition waste and natural fibers
researchUpdates.publicationStatus: Early-access accepted article; not final Version of Record
researchUpdates.authors: G. Murali, Luv Chaudhary, Patchamatla J. Rama Raju, Marzena Kurpińska, Leong Sing Wong, Jarosław Górski, Hakim S. Abdelgader, Shimol Philip and Siva Avudaiappan
researchUpdates.summary: Twenty mixtures combine recycled aggregates and natural fibers with waste-derived binders, linking impact experiments to statistical reliability and machine-learning analysis.
highlights: Increasing recycled aggregate content reduced impact resistance in the tested fiber mixtures.
Fiber additions moderated impact-result variability; prediction remained tied to the study dataset.
researchUpdates.access: Indexed publisher abstract only; direct access unavailable. Full methods, uncertainty and external validation were not audited. No independent replication, field qualification or unreported-age strength is established.

journalArticle.title: Impact variability is not general reliability
journalArticle.summary: Keep a model’s endpoint attached to its claims.
paragraphs: This study pairs impact measurements with reliability modelling. Our editorial takeaway: retain the loading protocol and distinguish first cracking from failure.
Neither reduced variability nor a fitted predictor supplies shear, flexural or field-service evidence. Future formulation advice needs property-specific tests and external validation.
